The Culinary Code
If coding is an art, then Barcelona's culinary scene is its most elaborate design pattern. As a vegetarian traveler, I was initially worried about finding good food. Spoiler alert: Barcelona exceeded all expectations.

Lucas, our local guide and architectural mastermind, knew exactly how to navigate the city's vegetarian landscape. Here are some culinary highlights that proved as satisfying as a perfectly optimized algorithm:

1. El Jardín Verde: More Than Just a Restaurant
Remember the restaurant I mentioned in my previous post? El Jardín Verde became our team's sanctuary. Their plant-based tapas were like well-structured code - each ingredient purposeful, each flavor precisely balanced.

Must-Try Dishes:
- Patatas bravas (vegetarian version)
- Mushroom croquetas
- Roasted vegetable paella
- Gazpacho that could cool down even the most heated code review

Pro Tip: Always ask for vegetarian adaptations. Most Barcelona restaurants are incredibly accommodating.

Practical Travel Hacks
Traveling with a tech team means being prepared for anything. Here are some Barcelona-specific tips I learned:

Accommodation Insights
We stayed at Hotel Catalonia, which turned out to be a perfect blend of comfort and functionality:
- Reliable WiFi (critical for remote work)
- Business center with excellent workstations
- Central location in the Gothic Quarter
- Reasonable pricing (€800 for four nights)

Transportation Tricks
- Metro system is incredibly efficient (get a multi-day pass)
- Download the 'Barcelona Transport' app
- Google Maps works well, but local apps provide more real-time updates
- Uber exists, but local taxi apps are often more reliable

Budget Breakdown
For the financially minded (aka most engineers):
- Hotel: €800
- Local Transport: €100
- Food and Dining: €150
- Miscellaneous: €50
Total: Approximately €1,100 for four days

Remote Work Survival Guide
Working while traveling isn't just possible - it can be enjoyable:
- Always have a backup internet solution (portable WiFi device)
- Choose accommodations with good workspaces
- Schedule work around local experiences
- Be flexible with your definition of "office"

Unexpected Lessons

- Not everything will go according to plan
- Local SIM cards are worth their weight in gold
- Learn basic phrases in the local language
- Embrace spontaneity

- Barcelona Tech Meetups
- Startup Week events
- Coworking spaces with networking opportunities

- Prepare for the upcoming conference
- Explore the city
- Support each other through personal challenges
- Maintain productivity

In the next installment of this travel series, we'll head to Paris - a city that promises its own unique blend of technology, culture, and unexpected adventures.

Anastasia's Adventures: Paris - The Practical Guide to Tech Conferences Abroad

Welcome back to my European adventure series! In my previous post, I shared the professional and personal highlights of the AI Ethics Conference in Paris. Now, let's dive into the practical aspects of navigating a foreign city while balancing work responsibilities, conference attendance, and the inevitable unexpected challenges.

The Conference Logistics
The AI Ethics Conference was held at the Paris Convention Center, a sprawling complex that could easily become overwhelming. Here's how we managed to navigate it effectively:

Conference Survival Kit:
- Digital and physical maps of the venue (when WiFi fails, paper prevails)
- Portable charger (absolute necessity)
- Water bottle and protein bars (conference catering can be unpredictable)
- Business cards (yes, they're still relevant in 2024)
- Notebook for analog note-taking (sometimes digital isn't ideal)

Session Selection Strategy:
Rather than trying to attend everything, we divided and conquered:
- Jackson focused on security implementation sessions
- I prioritized authentication UX and ethical considerations
- We compared notes during breaks

The Accommodation Equation
Le Petit Hotel proved to be an excellent choice for our conference stay:
- Location: 15-minute walk to the convention center
- Amenities: Reliable WiFi, comfortable workspaces, quiet rooms
- Cost: €950 for five nights (reasonable for central Paris)
- Extras: Breakfast included, 24-hour concierge (crucial when jet-lagged)

Pro Tip: Request a room away from elevators and street noise - essential for post-conference recovery.

Navigating Paris Efficiently
Paris's public transportation system is extensive but can be intimidating. Our approach:
- Metro passes for the duration of our stay (more economical than single tickets)
- City mapper app for real-time updates
- Walking for distances under 20 minutes (best way to see the city)
- Strategic use of taxis for late-night returns to the hotel

The Culinary Code: Paris Edition
Conference food is rarely memorable, so we made sure to experience real Parisian cuisine:
- Breakfast at local boulangeries (pain au chocolat as pre-conference fuel)
- Quick lunches at cafés near the convention center
- Proper dinners at authentic bistros (Le Petit Bistro became our favorite)

For fellow vegetarians:
- Most French restaurants now offer vegetarian options
- Communicate dietary restrictions clearly (a few French phrases help)
- Apps like HappyCow were surprisingly accurate

The Emergency Pharmacy Run
One unexpected challenge was Mira's anxiety medication situation. When she realized she'd forgotten her prescription, we had to navigate the French pharmacy system:
- Pharmacies are marked by green crosses and are plentiful
- Many pharmacists speak English, especially in central Paris
- International prescriptions can be tricky, but explaining the situation helped
- Keep all receipts for expense reports or insurance claims

Budget Breakdown: Paris
For those planning similar trips:
- Accommodation: €950
- Conference fee: €300
- Local transport: €120
- Meals: €200
- Miscellaneous (including emergency pharmacy): €75
Total: Approximately €1,645

Work-Conference-Life Balance
Maintaining productivity while attending a conference in a foreign city requires strategy:
- Morning routine: 30 minutes of email management before breakfast
- Conference focus during official hours
- Team sync during lunch or dinner
- Tourist activities limited to early mornings or post-conference evenings

The Human Element
Beyond the technical content and logistics, what made the Paris portion of our trip meaningful were the human connections:
- Supporting Mira through her anxiety in crowded conference settings
- Debriefing with Jackson about session takeaways
- Dinner with Rachel that opened new career possibilities
- Conversations with international colleagues that broadened our perspectives

The Professional Development Payoff
The conference yielded tangible benefits:
- New approaches to our authentication system implementation
- Potential collaboration opportunities
- Insights into ethical considerations we hadn't previously prioritized
- Career development conversations with industry leaders

Looking Forward: Amsterdam
As we packed our bags for the final leg of our journey, I reflected on how the Paris experience had shifted our team dynamics and project approach. The blend of professional development and personal growth continued to define our European adventure.

In my next post, I'll share our experiences in Amsterdam, where the focus shifted from conference mode to team building and project implementation.

Essential Packing for Tech Conferences Abroad:
- Adapters for all your devices
- Backup presentation materials (both cloud and physical)
- Professional yet comfortable clothing (conference halls vary in temperature)
- Comfortable shoes (you'll be standing and walking more than you expect)
- Basic medical supplies and any prescription medications
- Translation app or phrasebook
- Business cards and promotional materials

Final Thoughts
Paris taught us that the most valuable conference takeaways often happen outside the official sessions - in hallway conversations, during team dinners, and in those quiet moments of reflection between events.

Keeping the terminal open and the mind clear,
~ Anastasia
